Moist heatwave: Bihar’s next big summer threat
This is why the wet-bulb temperature, which combines air temperature and humidity, has become an important indicator of heat stress.
Bihar is particularly vulnerable to such conditions. Its location in the Gangetic plains, extensive agricultural landscape, high population density and large dependence on outdoor work expose millions to extreme heat.
The situation can become more complicated when hot conditions persist after the onset of moisture-laden winds or during the transition towards the monsoon.
Cities such as Patna, Gaya, Muzaffarpur and Bhagalpur may experience a combination of high temperatures and humidity, creating oppressive conditions for students, workers, farmers, street vendors and construction workers. Poor ventilation in houses and classrooms can further increase indoor heat stress.
A moist heat wave can affect more than physical health. It may reduce concentration, cause
For Bihar, therefore, heatwave preparedness cannot depend solely on maximum temperature forecasts. Weather warnings should increasingly communicate humidity, heat index and wet-bulb conditions. Schools and colleges could adjust outdoor activities and examination schedules during periods of severe heat stress, while cities need more shaded spaces, drinking-water points, trees and well-ventilated public buildings.
Patna University geology teacher Bhavuk Sharma said a moist heatwave is more dangerous than a dry one because high humidity reduces the body’s ability to cool through sweating. It may cause heat exhaustion, dehydration, dizziness and fatigue, while prolonged exposure can lead to heatstroke, cardiovascular stress, reduced productivity and increased risks for elderly people and children.

title: Sonu Sood reaches out to flood-hit people in Begusarai - The Times of India
full_text:
Sonu Sood reaches out to flood-hit people in Begusarai
He met residents, particularly children, and interacted with them. Speaking to the media, Sood said, “People of the state are extremely hardworking. They are resilient enough to come over this calamity. However, we have the duty to provide them a hand of help during their difficult time.”
He said the state govt was doing an extremely good job in relief and rescue. “Yet, the government must take concrete measures to stop frequent recurrence of flood in the state and provide a permanent solution,” he said.
The foundation distributed 10,000 packets of dry food. Sood later visited flood-affected areas of Teghra block before leaving for Lakhisarai.
